title: Pre-Analysis — Interim Filter and Seal Kit for the Nose Wheel Steering Manifold
abstract: Re-analysis of the interim steering filter kit opened when the permanent manifold reached production, to decide whether the interim standard should be withdrawn or left available for aircraft that will never be converted.

sections.objective: With the machined manifold cut into production and its retrofit bulletin issued, the question was whether the interim filter and seal kit should be withdrawn. Roughly a third of the affected population is expected to leave service before a base maintenance visit long enough to take the permanent conversion, and those aircraft would be left with nothing if the interim kit went away.
sections.findings_summary: Three items were confirmed and the decision was delegated rather than taken. The interim bulletin remains the only published route for an aircraft that will not be converted, and its four thousand hour filter interval is written into the maintenance planning document; withdrawing it would leave that interval orphaned. The removal task calls the non-return valve up for cleaning rather than replacement, and that step exists only because of the interim kit. The third finding came from the semantic search and is worth recording: the engine driven pump case drain work on the same hydraulic system reads very much like this one and was raised for the same underlying reason, debris from the later pump standard, but shares no part and no FIN with it. The recommendation was to keep the interim kit available and to hand the withdrawal decision to the in-service fleet plan.
sections.next_steps: Keep the interim bulletin open and the kit available until the retirement plan for the unconverted population is firm. Ask the maintenance planning group to state the filter interval against the interim standard explicitly rather than against the aircraft. Hand the withdrawal decision to in-service engineering with the population figures attached.

tasks.title: Establish the published content that depends on the interim kit
Size the population that will not take the permanent conversion

expected_findings.rationale: The interim bulletin is the only published route for an aircraft that will not be converted, and its four thousand hour filter interval is written into the maintenance planning document. Withdrawing it orphans that interval.
expected_findings.resolution: Keep the bulletin open until the retirement plan for the unconverted population is firm.

expected_findings.rationale: The removal task calls the non-return valve up for cleaning rather than replacement, a step that exists only because of the interim kit.
expected_findings.resolution: Retain the step while the interim standard is in the field.

evidence.similarity_note: Both texts describe an answer to debris generated by a later pump standard on the same hydraulic system, in almost the same words, but they share no part number, no FIN and no zone.

expected_findings.rationale: The engine driven pump case drain work was raised for the same underlying reason and reads very like this modification, yet it touches a different part of the system entirely.
expected_findings.resolution: No action. Recorded because a reviewer will expect it to have been considered.

expected_non_findings.reason: Surfaced by the same debris wording and the same hydraulic system, but it embodies an interim shaft seal kit on the engine driven pump and shares no part, no FIN and no zone with the steering manifold.

type_data.conclusion: Closed by delegation. The interim standard cannot be withdrawn on engineering grounds alone; the decision belongs to the in-service fleet plan and was handed over with the population figures.
